name: Gale Crater
coordinate_note: Per-site numbers were collected by Hermes with source URLs and not independently re-checked by Claude. status=sourced means a URL exists; unverified means no published number was found (leave empty, do not estimate); weak_source means the only source is Wikipedia and should be replaced. Site coordinates are approximate and from memory: verify against the USGS Mars gazetteer before use.

facts.unit: m (lowest point of the NW floor per the paper; the Curiosity landing site is about -4,500 m in MOLA)

verified.detail: Cambridge paper: elevations range from -4670 m on the northwestern floor (MOLA areoid). Our MOLA DEM at the landing site is -4,500 m (min -4,607 m within 80 km). Value now states both.

facts.unit: m (paper text: ~5 km; MOLA suggests up to ~5.4-5.5 km)

verified.detail: Paper text says the central mound is ~5 km high; highest interior point 838 m above the areoid implies ~5.5 km from the -4670 m floor. Our MOLA max within 80 km is +771 m (~5.4 km).
Paper: Gale is ~154 km in diameter (Fig. 1 caption: 154 km).

Fergason/Gulick MSL workshop talk, Gale slide: mean TI 365, std 50. Our THEMIS 5x5 window at the landing coordinates reads 515 (448-654): different area and method, so the numbers are not interchangeable.

facts.unit: degC (REMS, winter night to summer afternoon)

verified.detail: JPL: 15.9 C on a summer afternoon to minus 100 C (-148 F) on a winter night.
The DOI resolves to an abstract that gives landing elevation and a sol-3967 position, no ground-temperature minimum or Ls; MDPI full text returned 403. Marked unverified until a source is found.

facts.value: Fe/Mg smectite clays below, hydrated Mg-sulfates above; hematite (~4-8 wt%) present throughout the clay-sulfate transition

verified.detail: Rampe+ 2022: hydrated Mg-sulfate layers overlie Fe/Mg smectite layers; hematite is present at ~4-8 wt% throughout the five transition samples, not a separate middle step.
